questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
1. Standard penetration test (SPT) is conducted by using split spoon sampler.
2. Dynamic cone penetration test for site investigation is based on the principle that elastic shock waves travel in different materials at different velocities.
3. Use of N-values not corrected for overburden pressure leads to highly conservative design of footing at shallow depths.
Which of the above statements are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
(c)
Standard Penetration Test (SPT) gives N-value which can be corrected for energy, overburden pressure and dilatancy in sequence. The corrected N-value is correlated with relative density and angle of shearing resistance for cohesionless soils; and unconfined compressive strength and consistency for cohesive soils.
Since the confining pressure increases with depth, the N values at shallow depths are underestimated
and the N values at larger depths are overestimated.

The following items consists of two statements, labelled as Statement I and Statement II. You have to examine the two statements and select your answer using the codes given below:
Codes:
(a) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I.
(b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I.
(c) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
(d) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Statement (I): The field consolidation curve is steeper than the laboratory curve.
Statement (II): Samples taken for laboratory test are subjected to disturbance.
questions.solution:
(a)
The disturbance of the soil sample used in the laboratory changes the structure of soil. Therefore
the field consolidation curve is steeper than laboratory consolidation curve for clay. The remoulding
of clay further reduces the compressibility and thus curve has least slope for remoulded soil

The following items consists of two statements, labelled as Statement I and Statement II. You have to examine the two statements and select your answer using the codes given below:

(a) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I.
(b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I.
(c) Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
(d) Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Statement (I): When a saturated soil mass is subjected to consolidation, its volume at any instant is related to the total stress.
Statement (II): Total stress is equal to the sum of the effective stress and pore water pressure.
questions.solution:
(d)
Volume of saturated soil sample at any time = (Initial thickness–Settlement) × Area of sample. The
volume is related to strain directly. The settlement depends on change in effective stress and not
on the change in total stress.

Statement (I): For over consolidated clays with OCR > 4, the ultimate bearing capacity for long term situation will be more than short term situation.
Statement (II): For long term condition, the pore water pressure dissipates.
questions.solution:
(d)
For overconsolidated clays with OCR greater than 4, long term ultimate bearing capacity will be
less because of negative pore water pressure induced during undrained shear which makes the
undrained shear strength of clay greater than the drained strength.

Statement (I): The failure envelope in terms of effective stress for sands is not a straight line.
Statement (II): Particles crushing occur at high stresses.
questions.solution:
(d)
The failure envelope in terms of effective stress for sands is a straight line but at high stresses,
when particles get crushed, the failure envelope becomes a gentle concave (downward) curve.
